A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have succeeded in the design and synthesis of amphiphilic norbornene-appen ded HBCs that self-assemble into covalently stabilized nanofibers with one-handed helical chiralities.
we have successfully designed a new class of amphiphiles, namely, Gemini-shaped hexabenzo-coronenes, and demonstrated their unique ability to self-assemble into graphitic nanostructures.
we have developed a new synthetic method for the construction of conductive one-handed helical nanostructures, which is based on the coassembly of a pair of Gemini-shaped HBC derivatives.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the coassembly of two different HBC molecules, which is based on a simple molecular recognition principle, provides a versatile and efficient approach to the construction of one-handed helical nanostructures that exhibit electroconductive behavior.
the coassembly of two different amphiphiles with different molecular shapes and/or sizes can be used as a powerful approach for the selective formation of helical nanocoils with one-handedness.
we have developed a method for the construction of a conductive one-handed helical nanostructure that is robust enough to be used for the exploration of its electromagnetic properties.
